raw_response:
I farm only 1.5 mu, so even though I understand the technical recommendations, I still make decisions like a smallholder first: I cannot tie up too much cash, and I cannot depend on everyone being home at the busy time. For me, the safest arrangement is still wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. Wheat-maize keeps grain coming in both seasons, spreads risk, and fits what has worked here in Quzhou. I have well irrigation, so I will use it, but not excessively because pumping costs money. On wheat I will put most of my attention into a stable stand, a solid base fertilizer, and a topdress at jointing if the crop looks strong enough to justify it. On maize, because the turnaround after wheat is very tight and some family members work off-farm, I will keep tillage simple and plant quickly with hybrid seed. I would rather spend a bit on seed and a moderate fertilizer rate than gamble on low input and lose yield. But on such a small area, I still keep the plan conservative and practical, not maximum-input.
